stories.headline: Lee Jae-myung nominates BIS economist Shin Hyun-song as Bank of Korea governor
stories.summary: President Lee nominated Shin Hyun-song, head of the Monetary and Economic Department at the Bank for International Settlements, as the new Bank of Korea governor to replace Rhee Chang-yong. Shin is known for predicting the 2008 financial crisis and takes a hawkish stance on monetary policy.

stories.headline: President Lee announces stock market reform measures to address Korea discount
stories.summary: President Lee unveiled capital market reforms including proposed bans on duplicate listings by conglomerates and faster T+1 settlement systems to address chronic undervaluation of Korean stocks. The announcement triggered a market rally and included meetings with investors and financial authorities.

stories.summary: President Lee's approval rating climbed to 67 percent, the highest since taking office, with economic management cited as the top driver of public support according to polling data from Gallup Korea.

stories.headline: Democratic Party passes prosecution reform bills after 24-hour filibuster
stories.summary: The ruling Democratic Party secured passage of prosecution reform bills establishing a new agency for investigating serious crimes with a 166-1 vote, ending a 24-hour filibuster by the opposition People Power Party. The reforms separate investigative and indictment powers.

stories.headline: Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon registers for People Power Party primary after delays
stories.summary: Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon finally registered his candidacy with the People Power Party for the June local elections after twice refusing to register. The decision came amid internal party strife over nomination processes and reform direction.
